observations: The final executable rendered Proxies at 960x640 and 520x520 CSS pixels in light theme and at 960x640 in dark theme.
Pool and Route dialogs rendered with initial focus, domain controls and trailing actions visible.
Actual Apply displayed applying state while mutation controls were disabled, then reached Ready/applied.
Actual right-click on the Custom Pool opened the anchored Edit/Delete context menu.
The final executable also opened the same context menu from the explicit left-click button and retained keyboard focus semantics.
An empty valid isolated AppState rendered the page-level empty Pool state and zero-node surface without synthetic product data.
Immediate PrintWindow captured the native WebView startup-loading frame; an isolated invalid primary and backup state produced stateUnavailable with the production retry UI.
Manual node-a to node-b completed through fixed owned Clash API PUT/GET read-back and displayed authoritative selected/running state.
A recoverable pre-stop Compiler failure preserved the same owned Ready child and displayed an error Notice.
Externally stopping the isolated owned child caused the existing runtime event to refresh Proxies from applied/running to pending/saved-only.
The isolated state was reset and no listener remained at fixed port 9090 after cleanup.
data_boundary: Repository-owned isolated fixtures only; screenshots and Evidence exclude subscription URLs, credentials, API secrets, runtime tags and generated core configuration.
